Based on recent event I want to inform everyone to think very carefully before buying property or planning to move to Yash Paradise. Certain society committee members, many of whom are retired police personnel, allow their close contacts to organize parties inside the society.

Loud DJ music is permitted at full volume until 5 a.m., with no consideration for residents, senior citizens, children, or students—even during board exam periods. Alcohol consumption is openly allowed within the society premises and surrounding areas.

In addition to this, water shortage is a regular and serious issue in the society. This problem occurs every month throughout the year, and it becomes especially severe from March to July, making daily life extremely difficult for residents.

Due to frequent disturbances and poor basic facilities, the society is not suitable for families. Overall management is weak, and the living conditions do not justify even a ₹10,000 rent.

Please evaluate all these points carefully before making any decision.

text.text:
The experience with the security staff and management here was extremely disappointing. Their behavior and language were highly unprofessional and disrespectful. They create their own rules and then apply them inconsistently, showing clear favoritism.

We were stopped for triple riding and were asked to pay a fine. We were willing to pay it. However, right in front of us, a person riding a scooter without wearing a helmet was stopped, and instead of being fined, they were simply told, "Please wear a helmet," and allowed to leave.

When we requested that one person get off the bike so only two of us would continue, we were told that we would not be allowed to leave unless we paid the fine. We were asked to speak to the manager. After waiting for about 15 minutes, the manager arrived and rudely said, "Do whatever you want," instead of addressing our concern professionally.

The security staff at the main gate behave with unnecessary arrogance and treat people disrespectfully. This kind of biased enforcement and poor management reflects very badly on the organization. Overall, it was a completely unacceptable and third-class experience.

The security here closes off the boundary gates of the footpath, so you're forced to walk through it all the way to exit. When you leave in the evening, as you walk through the footpath, you'd hear a common, periodic chant - "Tation! Tation! Tation!". The Auto wale uncles here are passionate and dedicated to one single task - to take you to the railway station, whether you like it or not. If you're a guy, they will pull you by your hand to take you to their autos, all while some try to grab you too to take you to THEIR autos. They don't even ask if you wish to go to the station or not. But looking at their passion, anyone will go with them even if their destination  isn't the station, such is the entrancing conviction they possess. To be honest, I love the attention. I mean, at least these auto walas want me, unlike all the past girls I have liked in my life...
If you're aboard one of these autos going to the "Tation", boy, are you in for a ride. The ability to drive more rashly than a drunk man while actually being sober is baffling. At first, you fear for your life. But once you're habituated to it, you learn to enjoy the thrill. Heck, if your corporate slave life has left you feeling dead inside, these auto rides will surely make you feel alive again.

text.text:
This place is my prison. It's just that my shackles are invisible. Everyday I am forced to come back here to give away my youth to work. How are the rest of you coping? Does it not get frustrating at some point? Doesn't it feel like everyday is on repeat? I get it, we've to do it for money. But still..

Maybe I really should quit my job. But preparing for interviews on the weekends is agony. I'm stuck in this corporate hell.

When I look down at the people from my office's glass window, they seem so miserable. Moving like ants in a line, desperate to return home to their families.

The beautiful sunsets and skies that you can view from here almost feels like a poetic joke made by the universe. For it's a stark contrast to the hell that is my work place. Still, it soothes me a little. I've attached a few photos of the sceneries for reference.
I've seen many seasons come and go here, be it rain, the scorching summer or the flimsy winter. The only thing that hasn't changed during this time is myself. I am still miserable.

Maybe computer engineering was a mistake. I don't like it particularly in the first place. Everyone these days is a Software Engineer. Hearing that title makes me cringe inside, like the bad aftertaste of a medicine. It's so boring that everyone around is a software engineer. Why don't I get to meet people who say "I am a psychologist" or "I am a writer" or something cool like that?

Is a so called stable job that important? Stability, but at what cost? Your whole mental health? How does it feel to have become a human whose primal fear is not heights, not a wild animal, not death, but something as lame as a Monday?

Even as I say this, I know that I need to go back to this place. I need to earn. Money is happiness, after all. But we are working everyday for someone else's dream; someone we don't even know, a system who doesn't even know or care about your existence.

Just like Sisyphus, I keep doing this meaningless task, apparently forever.

Apart from all that, the infrastructure and maintenance here is good 😊 The restrooms are hygienic as well.

P.S. I thought this review was really funny but sadly I think it got taken down :( Hence, posting this again.

Buying a home is rarely a smooth journey, so I was pleasantly surprised by how straightforward and well-managed this entire experience turned out to be. From the initial discussion to the final stages, the booking process was transparent, structured, and refreshingly stress-free.

The team was consistently professional, approachable, and responsive. Every query—small or large—was addressed patiently, communication was clear, and timelines were respected. There were no last-minute surprises or shifting goalposts, which went a long way in building trust.

The project itself is very well executed and competitively priced for the Bandra–BKC location. Construction quality, planning, and overall finishing reflect attention to detail and seriousness of intent. What truly stood out was that the project was delivered well before the committed timeline—something that has become increasingly rare in today’s real estate landscape.

Overall, this has been a genuinely positive and reassuring experience. Credit to the builder and the entire team for delivering on their promises with professionalism and integrity. I would comfortably recommend them to anyone looking for quality execution, reliability, and peace of mind in a home purchase.

text.text:
This is by far the WORST and most pathetic society I have ever come across! 🤦🏻‍♂️
There are so many problems in this building, yet the broker conveniently hides all the issues and assures you that everything is fine just to get you to rent a flat. Once you move in and the problems start surfacing, you are left to deal with everything on your own. There is absolutely no one willing to listen or help!

Here are some of the major problems with this society:
👉🏻 Poor cleanliness and hygiene: The society is not cleaned properly. There is garbage and dirt everywhere.

👉🏻 A serious stray dog menace: Having pet dogs is perfectly fine, but this society is infested with stray dogs. They can attack you at any time. I have personally been attacked twice while jogging in the morning! And guess what? There is nobody to listen to your complaints or take any action. Every night, 50–60 dogs bark and fight continuously, making it almost impossible to sleep peacefully. There is no one to control the situation.

👉🏻 Absolutely NO mobile network: No mobile network from any telecom company works properly anywhere in the society. Without a Wi-Fi connection, your mobile phone is practically useless here. If you need to make a call, you have to go to the balcony and try your luck. If someone calls you, the call simply won't connect. You can only communicate if they contact you through WhatsApp calls or messages over Wi-Fi.

👉🏻 An unacceptable and ongoing water supply crisis: I rented a flat here in March, and by April 20, the water supply to the washrooms had completely stopped. Water was available only in the kitchen. Initially, I thought it would be a temporary issue, so I shifted to a hotel. I spent seven days there, but when the water supply still hadn't resumed, I was forced to return to the flat.
For three continuous months, not a single drop of water came into the washrooms! Imagine having to fill buckets in the kitchen and carry them to the washrooms just to manage basic daily needs. 🤦🏻‍♂️
The water supply resumed around June 23–24, but that didn't last either. From June 23–24 until today, October 28, water has been available for barely 24–25 days in total! They supply water to the washrooms for one day and then shut it off for the next four or five days. This ridiculous cycle continues even today.

👉🏻 Security concerns and an unresponsive management: Security in this society seems to have been left entirely to fate. The management simply refuses to listen to residents' complaints. It feels as though nobody is willing to take responsibility or address even the most basic problems.

MY ADVICE TO ANYONE CONSIDERING BUYING OR RENTING A FLAT HERE: Please think twice before making a decision. If you are prepared to put up with all these problems, you are welcome to move in. Otherwise, stay as far away from this society as possible!

A home should provide peace, safety, and basic necessities-not constant stress, sleepless nights, water shortages, and helplessness.

BEWARE! Do your own research and thoroughly check everything before committing to a flat here. 🙏🏻

text.text:
D-WING BUYERS, STAY ALERT!
To anyone considering this project, think carefully before investing your hard-earned money in Dynamix Group's project.

DYNAMIX GROUP HAS FOOLed THE PUBLIC ONCE AGAIN! 😂😂

Dynamix Group has once again obtained an extension from MahaRERA, pushing the possession deadline to 30th April 2027!

Let’s look at how C-Wing buyers have been misled time and again.

The flats were sold with a promise of possession by March 2025. When that deadline passed, buyers were told to expect possession by March 2026, as per the RERA timeline. March 2026 came and went, but there was still no possession.

Then came another promise: August 2026 — confirmed possession! Instead, the possession deadline was extended to December 2026. And now, once again, buyers are facing another extension, this time until 30th April 2027!

So, when will buyers actually get possession? May 2027? June 2027? Or will they have to wait until December 2027? Who knows! 😂

The biggest irony is that buyers paid for a brand-new property, but by the time they finally receive possession, it may feel like they're getting a second-hand property!

The entire structure was reportedly completed back in 2023. Since then, the building has been standing there, while buyers continue waiting for their homes. It feels as though the builder has collected the money but has no intention of handing over possession anytime soon!

God only knows what else C-Wing buyers will have to go through.How long are homebuyers supposed to keep waiting after repeatedly being given new possession deadlines? 🤦‍♂️😂

Dynamix Group, don’t bother replying to my comment because I already know what your response will be: “We are working tirelessly to hand over possession within the RERA timeline.”

But what you won’t mention is that you have already taken three extensions and given buyers three new deadlines! And as for your claim that you’re working tirelessly, what exactly have you been working tirelessly on, and since when? Only God knows! 😂😂😂

text.text:
Do Not Buy Any Flat in this building even if the flat is extremely cheap or say for free

The Builder of this building is Corporate thief.

Despite paying hefty advance maintenance, the residents alleged that they have been getting water supply for just 10-15 minutes a day, which is not enough for basic needs.

The compalints have been filed at Samta Nagar police station and the residents have alleged that they have been paying lakhs as maintenance fees but no basic facilities have been provided. UK Iridium is located in Kandivali East's Lokhandwala Township.

What have the residents complained?

Despite paying a hefty advance maintenance for the year October 2024–October 2025, the residents have been getting water supply for just 10-15 minutes a day, which is not enough for basic needs. A resident from the building also said that as “out of four water tanks, only one is functional." According to a report by Mid Day, the residents paid advance mainteinence of Rs 3.17 lakh for 1 BHK while Rs 3.54 lakh for 2BHK.

In addition to this, residents alleged that sewage drain water has also been entering the water tank. This is the water that is used for domestic purposes such as drinking, bathing and kitchen. Even though everyone has a filter at home, but for how long it will the filters be fit to for such drain water, questioned a resident.

Another major concern the residents have highlighted is fire safety. Many buildings in Mumbai have recently experienced fire problems, which have resulted in fatalities and injuries. A resident informed that fire safety norms have also been ignored, as fire duct have been filled with cement bags and debris while the staircases for emergency exit are locked.

Further adding, residents alleged that they were forced to take possession after the RERA extension expired. Residents also alleged that all ammenities such as swimming pool, gym charges, parking and garden are all on paper, however, none of it is provided by the builder.

text.text:
Let’s get straight to the point.

The only 4 or 5-star reviews you see here are from people who just saw the sample flat or interacted with the sales team. Some are probably old reviews too.

Every actual owner or tenant would give this place zero stars if that were possible.

Here’s why:

1. Cheap water pipelines were used. Bursts are common. I’ve posted pictures of the ones inside my flat. The ones outside affect the entire building.

2. There’s no staff to handle these issues. They haven’t been paid and are currently on strike.

3. The lifts are poorly programmed. One has been under construction for 4 to 5 months. Even with three working lifts, you still end up waiting 10 to 15 minutes.

4. The building entrance speaks for itself. Check the video I shared.

5. Parking is a mess.

6. The society still doesn’t have a proper gate.

7. There are daily water problems. Pipeline bursts have been happening constantly for the past four months, ever since I moved in.

8. No one listens to you in the facility office. All they say is “We’re working on it,” but nothing really changes.

9. There are leakages inside flats.

10. No proper electricity ducts. To install Wi-Fi, we had to run wires through whatever openings we could find, including fan holes.

11. Maintenance is terrible. You’ll see garbage lying on staircases.

12. Gutka stains in every lift.

I genuinely feel bad for the people who invested here. Many families are trying their best to make it livable — fixing leaks, dealing with water issues, coordinating with workers — things the management should have handled from the start.

If only the builders had focused on doing proper work instead of temporary patch-ups, this could have been a great place to live.

Right now, it just feels like a chawl pretending to be a high-rise.

text.text:
Lodha Amara is definitely one of the more premium and large-scale residential townships in Thane. The sheer size of the society is impressive. It almost feels like a mini city in itself, with everything planned within the campus.

One of the biggest highlights is the open space and greenery. The project is spread across a massive area with landscaped gardens, walking trails, and dedicated zones to relax, which gives it a refreshing and less congested feel compared to typical city societies.

The amenities are where it truly stands out. Multiple swimming pools, large playgrounds, and dedicated sports facilities like cricket and football turfs make it ideal for an active lifestyle. There are also multiple clubhouses, gym facilities, and recreational zones, so there’s always something to do within the society itself.

The community vibe is quite lively as well, with events and activities happening regularly, giving it a proper township feel rather than just a residential complex.

However, because of its scale, the society can feel extremely crowded at times. With a large number of buildings and residents, common areas and amenities can get busy, especially during peak hours. Some residents also feel that the flats are relatively compact for the price point.

Another point to consider is connectivity. While it is well-located in Thane, public transport access can still be a limitation depending on your daily commute.

Overall, Lodha Amara offers a premium lifestyle with extensive amenities and greenery. It’s a great choice if you enjoy a township-style living with everything inside, but the crowd density and compact living spaces might not suit everyone.

Disappointing Experience – Poor Facilities and Unresponsive Management
I stayed at The Bombay Home Company for a week, and unfortunately, it was one of the most frustrating hospitality experiences I’ve had.
For the first four days, the air conditioning and jet spray in the bathroom were not functioning — a serious issue given the sweltering summer heat in Mumbai. Despite repeated complaints, the issue remained unresolved. An electrician was sent, but the AC continued to malfunction, leaving me to sleep in an uncomfortably hot room night after night.
After several follow-ups, I was finally offered an alternative accommodation — but it was located 10 kilometers away. No shuttle or assistance was provided for the move, and I had to arrange and pay for transport myself. Upon arrival, I was shocked to find that the new place was not a proper Airbnb apartment, but rather a private room that had been hastily vacated for my stay.
The room reeked of cigarette smoke despite being advertised as non-smoking — a serious concern for someone like me with a smoke allergy. The toilet was unhygienic, the space was extremely cramped, and to make matters worse, the geyser didn’t work. When I reported this, I was told someone would come to fix it, but no one showed up even after an hour.
At that point, I decided to vacate the property and requested a refund for the remaining three days. Not only was my request denied, but the management also stopped responding altogether. When I pointed out that the amenities they failed to provide — working AC, geyser, clean and smoke-free room — were not in line with what was promised, they simply said it was “not in their policy” to offer refunds.
The overall experience was deeply disappointing — from the lack of basic amenities to the unprofessional and indifferent attitude of the staff. I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for a comfortable or reliable stay in Mumbai.

Also their sofa had a hole and nail in it which was not visible and i got hurt by that.

No shuttle or assistance was provided for the move, and I had to arrange and pay for transport myself. Upon arrival, I was shocked to find that the new place was not a proper Airbnb apartment, but rather a private room that had been hastily vacated for my stay.
The room reeked of cigarette smoke despite being advertised as non-smoking — a serious concern for someone like me with a smoke allergy. The toilet was unhygienic, the space was extremely cramped, and to make matters worse, the geyser didn’t work. When I reported this, I was told someone would come to fix it, but no one showed up even after an hour.
At that point, I decided to vacate the property and requested a refund for the remaining three days. Not only was my request denied, but the management also stopped responding altogether. When I pointed out that the amenities they failed to provide — working AC, geyser, clean and smoke-free room — were not in line with what was promised, they simply said it was “not in their policy” to offer refunds.
The overall experience was deeply disappointing — from the lack of basic amenities to the unprofessional and indifferent attitude of the staff. I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for a comfortable or reliable stay in Mumbai.

Also their sofa had a hole and nail in it which was not visible and i got hurt by that.

If there was a rating lesser than 1star, I would have used one to review this project. After thoughtful consideration, I am writing this review for the potential buyers planning to invest in Marathon projects.
I made an investment in the project in the year 2021 going by the project’s and the builder’s reputation.
The Committed possession timeline was Dec 2023. Let alone the possession of the property, there was no official communication of the delay in the handover.
After continuous followups, multiple visits and lots of to and fro I was handed over the property on 25 May 2024 with no water supply and electricity connection. I was requested to wait for couple more days after the possession to have the water supply and electricity enabled which obviously did not happen until another week.
Please note while signing the possession letter, I was told all the observation's identified during inspection has already been fixed,
Water supply and electricity is enabled but obviously that was not the case when the property was Handedover on 25th May 2024.
After the possession, there was leekages in washbasin area, drainage blockages which I had to get it coordinated with facility team myself.Trust me the process was no less than a nightmare.
I thought my case was exceptional, however I realised everybody who has invested in the project has encountered similar issues.
I am attaching the pictures for a clear-view of the quality which is been delivered under the premise of the brand value we were promised of.
Coming to the society premises, there is still flooring work going on in the lower floors, lobby, terrace. Amenities for which they have started charging us in the maintenance cost doesn’t exist.
We have been made to sign a consent letter/ no objection letter that the construction work will continue to happen till Dec 2024 while they have made us complete the possession process by an email confirmation of project completion by Jun 2024. While I want to be optimistic about the committed timelines, I am equally hopeless about any services or completion of the project in the near future.
I am attaching the project images when the flats has already been handed over for the reference.

text.text:
Review for Rustamjee Seasons, BKC

If you’re planning to rent or buy here, I’d strongly say: think twice.

The building looks great on the surface with every amenity listed—gym, pool, squash, TT, yoga rooms—but in practice, it’s a disappointment . Here’s why:
1.	Rigid and impractical rules:
•	Table tennis and squash are restricted with sudden, unclear rules—you can’t just go and play when you want.
•	Gym timings are extremely rigid. Management insists the gym cannot open early because the trainer isn’t available, but ironically, the trainer often shows up an hour late even after the gym has officially opened. Makes no sense.
2.	Amenities without basics:
•	The pool is there, but essential float boards or safety equipment are missing. It’s incomplete and not child-friendly.
3.	Hidden charges everywhere:
•	Even after paying steep rents, almost everything is chargeable—yoga rooms, certain common spaces, and more. Feels unfair and exploitative considering the rent is already high.

On top of this, the hygiene is terrible (toilets stink worse than public ones), lifts are painfully slow, and the management is neither flexible nor approachable. If you’re a tenant, your say is practically zero. Even flat owners don’t have much control since the committee runs on its own agenda. And yes parking is scary-no space to even get into the car-forget your car even being cleaned . I think the list is never ending!

Yes, it’s one of the few residential complexes in BKC, but amenities you can’t use and management you can’t reason with cancel out any advantage.

Verdict: Not worth the rent, not worth the stress. Big no from my side.

My experience with Mahindra Alcove has been disappointing, especially considering the amount of money being spent on these apartments.

The nearby road frequently experiences heavy traffic, which makes commuting inconvenient and creates a lot of noise and congestion.

Overall, considering the high prices running into lakhs and crores, I expected significantly better construction quality and living conditions. In my experience, the project does not feel worth the amount being charged.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend buying or renting a property here.

text.text:
Total letdown from a brand that sells itself on trust and credibility

I booked at Mahindra Alcove based on the possession timelines repeatedly communicated by the sales team. Those commitments have proven completely unreliable, with possession for Wings A now delayed by almost two years.
What's even more disappointing is that amenities like the swimming pool had not even started, raising serious concerns about the actual timeline for project completion.
A home is not just a financial investment, it carries immense emotional value. Looking back, trusting the Mahindra brand feels like a mistake.

As per applicable laws and customer commitments, buyers like me who continue to bear EMIs, rent, and other costs because of such delays deserve compensation. Accountability cannot be one-sided.

I honestly wish I could give negative stars.

And before the standard response arrives asking for my contact number and email address, let me save everyone the trouble. Many buyers have already shared their details and received little clarity. Instead of asking customers to contact you, please answer publicly:
• Why did the sales team make promises that were clearly unrealistic?
• Why is the Customer Relationship team often dismissive of genuine customer concerns?
• What is the actual possession date for Wings A & B?
• What compensation will buyers receive for this prolonged delay?

We deserve transparency, not generic template responses.

Update (14th Nov 2026): Still no clear possession date in sight plus the following incidence:

I am here at the property and wanted to see the status live for my flat. There have been multiple instances of timeline lapse from your end which is pathetic in itself and now you are not even allowing to check the status to the property owner. What non-sense is this.

Let me know if I need to escalate this and file an official complaint against the entire project. This is pathetic customer support. Firstly, the timeline committed from your end is never maintained and then this pathetic stuff.

I am here at the property coming from afar and really wanted to check the status of my flat for myself.

text.text:
Very disappointing to give a 1-star rating. When I initially booked, I had a high rating as first time experience in mind. Unfortunately, my interactions and follow-ups over the past year have only resulted in false promises and repeated delays, seemingly just to buy time.

In December 2025, during discussions with their CRM representative, Meghana, I was at least assured that the delay would come with some form of compensation as per the agreement. However, a month later, that assurance appeared to be nothing more than a temporary reassurance. A new CRM representative was introduced, and any prior commitments were completely denied.

This reflects poorly on Mahindra, and such practices have completely shattered the trust my family and I had when we made the booking.

As customers, we are clearly not treated as the priority. Builders seem to hold all the power—but with such practices, they risk losing credibility and long-term trust.

One simple question remains:
If a customer delays a payment milestone, interest is charged daily without exception. Why, then, is the builder not equally accountable to pay compensation when the delay is on their end?

Still waiting—and counting the days for long awaited possession.

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ A place that genuinely feels like home
What I really like about Shapoorji Pallonji Vicinia is that the planning feels different from many other high-rise projects. The apartments are spacious, thoughtfully laid out and designed to make good use of every corner. Most importantly, the orientation gives you a great sense of privacy — homes don’t directly face each other, so you’re not looking into your neighbour’s living room. That’s a small but brilliant design detail.
The views, greenery and open spaces add to the experience, and the amenities are excellent — pool, gym, jogging/cycling track, tennis, badminton, squash, basketball, box cricket, kids’ play areas and indoor games.
What stands out for me is the combination of larger rooms, privacy, greenery and a genuinely well-planned community. It doesn’t feel like just another apartment complex; it feels like a place where you’d actually enjoy living.
Vicinia gets the basics right, and the little details make it special. ❤️

Views from apartments attached.

⭐ 1/5 — Extremely disappointing experience. Think twice before buying here.

In my personal experience as a former resident, Kalpataru Vienta has been an extremely disappointing place to live, and I would strongly advise prospective buyers to do extensive due diligence before investing here.

The lift situation is absolutely unacceptable. At times, residents can spend around 30 minutes waiting for a lift. For a premium residential building, this is simply not the standard I expected. The lifts themselves have no proper ventilation or fan, and the lobby also has poor ventilation and airflow. ACs have been installed in the lobby, but in my experience, they are frequently not functioning.

The management and staff experience has been equally frustrating. I found the staff to be rude on multiple occasions, and my experience with the management committee was even more disappointing. Complaints and concerns did not feel like they were being taken seriously.

I was particularly disappointed with the functioning of the committee under Chairman Mr. Vimal Shah. In my opinion, the committee’s approach has been extremely unresponsive and residents deserve much better accountability, transparency and communication.

Maintenance charges are another major concern. The maintenance for my 2BHK was approximately ₹12,000 under the builder, and under the current management it increased to approximately ₹15,000 for a 2BHK. Given the overall condition and services, I personally found this increase difficult to justify.

The build quality has also been a major disappointment. Leakage and seepage have been recurring concerns, and I have seen such issues affecting multiple flats. For a building marketed at a premium level, this is extremely disappointing.

The amenities are not as impressive as they may initially appear. Once you actually live here, the maintenance and day-to-day experience can be very different from what you see during a sales visit. Cleanliness is also an issue, with garbage visible in various areas, which further affects the overall experience.

I eventually sold my flat, and honestly, I am thankful that I was able to exit the property. That decision was based on my own experience and overall satisfaction with the building.

If you are considering buying here, please don’t rely only on the sales presentation or the appearance of the property. Visit the building at different times, speak privately with existing residents, check the lifts during peak hours, ask about seepage/leakage problems, verify the maintenance charges and understand how the management handles resident complaints.

For me personally, living here was a very disappointing experience, and I would not buy a flat in this building again.

Buying from Lodha has been one of the most disappointing experiences. Our flat (Tower 1) was promised for December 2025, but they have now pushed possession to December 2026 without any solid explanation. Their team is unresponsive, careless, and arrogant. Getting a straight answer from them is nearly impossible.

They keep pretending to be a “brand,” but the reality is far from it. The entire experience feels like dealing with a local builder wrapped in marketing gloss. There is no professionalism, no accountability, just endless excuses and empty promises.

At one point, they even raised payment demands before actually achieving the promised milestones. It was so blatant that even their own on-ground staff seemed embarrassed by the lies. That moment said everything about how Lodha operates.

Many of us have already paid over 95 percent of the total amount, yet there is still no clarity on

Updating on July 2026:

I went to their site and talked to the sales folks. They don't have any update and they would speak very cleverly with a "term" in "as if now"  we have no intimation from the builder. You might receive your flat by the end of the year but that is "as if now".

If some intimation comes we will let you know but these liars will not inform you.

When I went and checked the RARA status of the project, the builder has applied for an extension of one year.  the RARA has been shifted from 28th Feb 2027 to 28th Feb 2028. The builder had promised us to hand over that in December 2025 so it's a good delay of three years.

I'm just posting it for whosoever is affected. Please don't relay on Builders notification. Check RERA website.

⭐ 1-Star Review

If you're planning to buy a flat or rent an apartment in Paradise Sai Crystals, Sector 35D, my sincere advice is to speak to the current residents before making any decision. Don't be influenced by the building's appearance or by positive online reviews alone.

Based on my personal experience, this society has several ongoing issues. There are frequent water supply problems and regular electricity-related issues. Most of the amenities are poorly maintained and are often not in usable condition.

One of the biggest concerns is the lift. One of the lifts is frequently out of service for long periods, forcing everyone to depend on a single lift. Even after raising complaints, there is little to no effective action or timely resolution.

Overall, my experience has been extremely disappointing. If you value your peace of mind, I would strongly recommend doing thorough research and speaking to existing residents before deciding to buy or rent here. Don't make your decision based only on the building's appearance.

This review reflects my personal experience and is intended to help others make an informed decision.

​I am writing to express my extreme disappointment and register a formal complaint regarding gross misrepresentation and unethical sales practices during the booking of our two 1BHK apartments in Tower 2.
​Our booking was handled by your sales representative, Kamna. At the time of booking, we were explicitly assured of a March 2026 possession timeline. This date has since been deferred to September 2026, causing considerable inconvenience.
​Furthermore, during the initial sales consultations, I specifically enquired about car parking provisions. Kamna explicitly assured me that while there would be no dedicated or allotted parking spaces for 1BHK units, open parking would be strictly available on a "first-come, first-served" basis. Based entirely on this assurance, my family proceeded with the booking.
​I have recently learned that this information was entirely false. I am now being informed that there is absolutely no provision for car parking for 1BHK residents, and that we are expected to rent parking spaces privately from 2BHK owners.
​When I confronted Kamna regarding this contradiction, she blatantly denied ever making the commitment, effectively dismissing a core condition upon which our purchase decision was made. This is a clear case of fraudulent misrepresentation and a severe breach of trust.

I am currently staying on rent at Lodha Crown Quality Homes, and my overall experience has been quite good.

The homes are well-designed with efficient use of space, and the infrastructure is modern and well-maintained. The society is clean, organized, and offers a wide range of amenities including a clubhouse, gym, steam room, swimming pool, kids’ play area, yoga and meditation spaces, parking facilities, a turf ground for cricket and football, and a badminton court. These facilities make day-to-day living comfortable and active.

There are a few areas that could be improved. The clubhouse facilities remain closed on Mondays, which can be slightly inconvenient. The swimming pool is cleaned regularly, but it would benefit from more rigorous maintenance. The steam room seems to be under maintenance most of the time, which limits its usability. The changing rooms also need better management and upkeep. Additionally, the parking tower lift is quite slow, which can be a bit frustrating during peak hours.

That said, the apartments can feel a bit small for a family of four. However, for bachelors or individuals, it works perfectly well and offers a convenient and hassle-free living experience.

Overall, a good option for rental living, especially for working professionals or bachelors looking for a well-managed and secure environment, with some scope for improvement in amenities maintenance.

I recently visited Lodha Park in Worli, and I must say, it is truly impressive. The ambiance of the place is nothing short of luxurious, with meticulous attention to detail in every aspect. The entire building exudes a sense of elegance and comfort, making it one of the finest residential options in the area.

The cleanliness of Lodha Park is outstanding. The staff is exceptionally good, always alert and conscious of their duties. They ensure that every corner of the property is spotless and well-maintained, adding to the overall appeal of the place.

One of the standout features of Lodha Park is its extensive range of amenities. There are 3 towers spread across 17 acres of land. The cricket ground, club house, and luxurious pools provide residents with plenty of options for recreation and relaxation. The high-speed lifts make accessing the 65 floors quick and convenient, reflecting the modernity and efficiency of the building. Parking is ample and well-organized, which is a big plus for residents with vehicles.

The greenery around Lodha Park is another highlight. The lush surroundings and scenic beauty create a serene and peaceful environment, which is quite rare in a bustling city like Mumbai. It’s a perfect place for families to enjoy nature while being in the heart of the city. The canteen is an added convenience, offering a variety of food options for residents.

Overall, Lodha Park stands out as one of the best places for a family to live. The combination of luxury, cleanliness, excellent staff, and top-notch amenities makes it a premier choice in Worli.

​The Views: The panoramic vistas of the Racecourse and the Arabian Sea are breathtaking. Watching the sunset over the Mumbai skyline from the floor-to-ceiling windows never gets old.

​If you are looking for the perfect blend of prestige, comfort, and a central location that connects you to South Mumbai’s pulse, One Lodha Place is the gold standard. It’s a vertical masterpiece that truly redefines luxury living in Mumbai.
​Highly recommended for those who appreciate the finer things in life!

I strongly advise anyone considering purchasing or renting a flat in any project by this builder to think very carefully before investing their money.

I have been living in Paradigm Antalya just opposite this project by the same builder for only two months, and the experience has been extremely disappointing. The building suffers from serious design, construction, and management issues that make daily living difficult.

The biggest problem is the severe water shortage. Residents receive water for only a very limited period( only 1 or 2 hours) each day, making basic household activities a constant struggle. Despite repeated complaints, there appears to be no adequate solution in place.

The building also has multiple construction and architectural flaws. There are water leakages, poorly planned utility areas, and extremely impractical installations. For example, the washing machine connection is located in such a way that residents may have to remove the entire door frame just to install a standard washing machine.

One of the most concerning issues is security. The duct area is easily accessible, and there are no proper stairs or secure access controls. In my own case, a plumber entered through the duct area to inspect a leakage and was able to access and record video footage of my bathroom from that area. This raises serious concerns about privacy and resident safety.

Management is equally disappointing. Calls and complaints often go unanswered, and residents are left to deal with problems on their own. Many owners and tenants in the building have expressed frustration and regret over their decision to move here, and some tenants have reportedly left shortly after moving in because of the living conditions.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend investing in this builder's projects. Prospective buyers should thoroughly investigate the quality of construction, water supply arrangements, security measures, and management standards before making any financial commitment.

text.text:
Marathon Nexzone – A Well-Planned Urban Township That Feels Like a City Within a City

Marathon Nexzone is one of the more thoughtfully planned residential townships in Navi Mumbai. The scale of the development itself is impressive, with tall towers arranged around open internal spaces that create a strong sense of community rather than feeling congested.

What stands out immediately is the open central area, which works well as a social and recreational hub—especially in the evenings. There’s good activity without chaos, making it suitable for families, working professionals, and seniors alike. The lighting at night is well done, adding to both safety and aesthetics.

Infrastructure & Living Experience:
The buildings are modern, and the layout allows decent airflow and light. Common areas appear well-maintained, and internal roads are wide enough to manage daily movement smoothly. Security presence and gated access add to peace of mind.

Amenities & Lifestyle:
The township offers multiple lifestyle conveniences within walking distance—play areas for kids, seating zones, and space to relax or socialize. It genuinely reduces the need to step out frequently for everyday recreation.

Kids & Family Friendly:
Very family-oriented. Kids have open spaces to play, and parents can comfortably supervise without traffic worries inside the complex.

Accessibility:
Lifts, ramps, and wide pathways make the complex fairly accessible for seniors and people with mobility needs.

Overall, Marathon Nexzone delivers a balanced urban living experience—modern, community-focused, and practical. A solid choice for anyone looking for a self-contained residential ecosystem in this part of the city.

Apart from experiencing the hospitality extended at the sales office, please also visit the facility management office before making any payment to the builder, as you will have to deal with that office after possession.

text.text:
Extremely disappointing experience with Sienna D Wing. Buyers should do thorough due diligence

My experience purchasing a flat in Sienna D Wing has been extremely disappointing and has caused me significant financial and emotional stress.

I purchased the flat from seller Manoj Sinha, through Rudra Properties / broker Harsh Adhya. Before completing the transaction, both the seller and broker represented to me that the project was nearing possession/completion and that possession was expected within approximately 8-10 months. The project was presented to me as being substantially close to completion.

I relied on these representations while making one of the biggest financial decisions of my life.

However, the reality after the purchase has been completely different.

The original project completion/possession timeline was December 2025, while the revised completion date is now shown as June 2027. Even more concerning, based on the construction progress I have personally observed, I have serious doubts about whether the project will actually be ready even by the revised date.

Despite the project not being ready for possession, I was made to pay 100% of the consideration for the flat, even though approximately 75% was due according to the builder's payment schedule at that stage, as I understood it. I was therefore left having paid essentially the entire amount while the construction remained substantially incomplete.

The seller received the full consideration and the broker received his brokerage, while I was left carrying the financial burden and dealing with the consequences of the delay.

What is particularly frustrating is that the information and assurances I received before the purchase gave me a completely different impression of the project's actual status. Had I been properly informed about the realistic construction position and the likely delay, I would have approached the transaction very differently.

My experience with Rudra Properties and broker Harsh Adhya has been particularly disappointing. I expected the broker to properly represent my interests and provide an accurate picture of the project before such a major transaction was completed. Instead, I feel that the focus throughout the transaction was on completing the sale.

The same applies to my experience with the seller, Manoj Sinha. I relied on the representations made to me regarding the project's progress and expected possession, but what I experienced after completing the purchase was very different.

From my experience, it felt as though everyone's priority was getting the transaction completed and receiving their money, while the consequences of the delayed project were left for the buyer to deal with.

I am posting this review because I genuinely wish I had done much deeper independent due diligence before purchasing.

Future buyers should not rely only on verbal assurances that a project is "near possession." Check the actual construction progress yourself, verify the MahaRERA records, revised completion dates, approvals, payment schedule and pending work, and speak to existing purchasers before committing such a large amount of money.

This review reflects my personal experience and the representations made to me during my transaction. I hope prospective buyers carefully investigate everything before making the same mistake I feel I made.

Siennaa by SD Corp in Kandivali East has been an absolute nightmare for homebuyers. When I booked my flat, the RERA completion date was December 2023. Then it quietly got pushed to 2024, then 2025, then 2026, and now it shows 2027. Every year they keep changing the timeline with zero accountability or real progress on-site.

Now, on top of all this, they have started asking homeowners to pay PMI even though the project is far from completion. It is unbelievable and completely unfair.

What really shocks me is how RERA keeps approving these extensions. The whole point of RERA was to protect homebuyers, not to shield builders who keep missing deadlines. But clearly, it seems like everyone is getting their fair share while buyers are left to suffer.

It feels like a scam at this point, with endless delays, no transparency, and no one holding the builder responsible. Think twice before investing your hard-earned money here.

🚨 Buyer Beware: Horrible Experience with this Developer in Bandra East.
I am writing this review to alert and warn potential homebuyers to be extremely cautious before dealing with this builder. We purchased a 2 BHK flat in what was marketed as a "premium project" in Bandra East, Mumbai, but our entire journey has been nothing short of a nightmare.Here is a detailed breakdown of why you should think twice before investing your hard-earned money with them:Delayed Possession Despite Full Payment: We bought a ready-to-move property and cleared the entire payment on time. Despite this, the builder delayed handing over possession by several months. Once they receive your money, they will literally make you beg for your own house.Illegal Maintenance Charges: Unfairly and unethically, they charged us maintenance fees for the period before they even handed over possession to us.Abysmal After-Sales & Professionalism: The sales and Customer Relation (CR) teams are highly unprofessional and extremely rude. Once the sale is closed, their attitude completely changes. Shockingly, they use goons (gundas) in their facility management team to threaten residents who raise legitimate complaints.Terrible Construction Quality & Immediate Damages:Leaks & Structural Cracks: Within just 2 months of moving in, severe water leakage started, and visible cracks developed on the walls.Cracked Doors: The doors provided were cracked. The builder promised to replace them before possession, but it has not been done to date.Cheap Materials: The builder used incredibly poor-quality electrical switches and faulty wiring throughout the flat.Unfit Possession Conditions: On the day of possession, the flat was left completely filthy and uncleaned. The developer refused to clean it, forcing us to hire an external professional cleaning agency at our own expense.Substandard Finishes: The painting work was of horrific quality. It looked so bad that we had to repaint the entire house out of our own pocket.False Promises on Amenities: The premium amenities proudly showcased in their sales brochure have either not been provided or are nowhere near the promised standard.
Final Verdict: Do not get fooled by their "premium project" branding or glossy brochures. This builder delivers sub-standard quality, zero customer service, and uses intimidation tactics. Save your peace of mind and your money—look elsewhere.

text.text:
I have booked a 2 BHK in tower 2B Auriga and I'll share my honest review. At first I was pretty optimistic about the project since it offers good amenities at a competitive price compared to projects by other builders in the area. But in the past 1 year the pace of construction has suffered tremendously. The builder has failed to deliver tower 1A and 1B possession within the RERA timeline and is set to default on the timeline for tower 2B as well (delay of 6 months over RERA deadline).

But my dissatisfaction peaked when I realised that the CRMs had been lying about the construction progress of tower 2B Auriga, they said the tiling flooring work has been completed up to the 16th floor whereas when I personally went and checked (they denied access to buyers, but I still managed to sneak in) it was not complete even up to the 6th floor. I am disappointed with the quality of the bathroom door provided in my apartment by Piramal.

The bottom portion of the bathroom door has developed fungus and significant deterioration. I raised the issue with the service team expecting it to be addressed as a quality/defect concern.

However, the response received from the official Piramal team was that the damage occurred due to “excessive and repeated exposure to water” during usage and cleaning, and therefore they would not provide support.

I find this explanation quite disappointing. A bathroom door is naturally expected to come in contact with water and moisture during bathroom usage and cleaning. If exposure to water causes the door to develop fungus and deteriorate, it raises serious concerns about the quality of the material, waterproofing, sealing, or finishing used.

For a reputed builder like Piramal, I would expect significantly better quality of material and workmanship, particularly in a premium residential project.

I am sharing photographs of the damaged door along with the official response received from Piramal so that prospective buyers/residents can make an informed assessment while purchasing property from piramal.

I hope Piramal reviews such quality issues more seriously and provides an appropriate resolution rather than attributing the deterioration to normal bathroom usage.

text.text:
My experience at Mayfair The View, Mumbai

**Pros:**
The location is good if your work is in Vikhroli. A nursery is nearby, mechanic shops are right outside the building, and the area is quite airy. Car and scooter mechanics are easily available nearby. Powai is close by, D-Mart is nearby, R City Mall is nearby, and there is an open market within walking distance where you can find almost everything you need.

Poptates is right in front of the building, so you can easily schedule meetings there or enjoy family dinners. The best part is the connectivity to Thane, Navi Mumbai, and South Mumbai through the Eastern Freeway, which can save around 40 minutes of travel time. BMC swimming pools are also nearby. The society uses the MyGate app, and maids are easily available. It's a single-tower society, so there are comparatively fewer people than in larger complexes.

**Cons:**
If you are a tenant, you have made a mistake. Neither the community members nor the society will respect you the same way they respect flat owners. At certain times, you will feel looked down upon.

There are too many cockroaches in almost every flat. Water leakage is a major issue, especially above the 20th floor, and you will often find water dripping from somewhere. It is a majority Muslim community building, so consider whether that suits you and your family.

There is absolutely no dedicated parking for two-wheelers inside the building. You have to find your own parking spot, people may scratch your vehicle, and on top of that, you still have to pay ₹500 as a parking charge.

Car parking is very expensive. If you park outside, BMC is usually not a major issue, but finding a parking spot after work can be difficult. If you go out for dinner, chances are your parking spot will be taken by the time you return, forcing you to use a taxi instead.

**Worst Broker Vivek & Landlord Experience**

My experience with broker Vivek Oberoi and the owner was extremely disappointing. While showing the flat, several issues were not disclosed. I was told there would be no move-in/move-out charges, but deductions were made later anyway.

The flat was handed over in a very dirty condition despite claims that it had been deep cleaned. I had to spend my own money cleaning the kitchen, washroom, and appliances.

Later, when I vacated the flat, they deducted ₹38,000 from my security deposit. When I questioned the deductions, Vivek told me to take the remaining amount or risk not getting that back either.

Vivek had earlier agreed to give me a ₹10,000 discount on his brokerage, but later, after teaming up with the owner, they deducted ₹10,000 from my security deposit instead.

They deducted ₹10,000 for painting the room. I offered to get the painting done myself, but they refused and said they would do it according to their own choice.

They also deducted ₹7,000 as a move-out charge, even though both the broker and owner had told me earlier that since I was taking a fully furnished flat, such charges would not be required. Later, they deducted it from my security deposit anyway.

They deducted ₹2,500 for scooter parking even though the building never asked me for it. It felt like they simply kept that amount for themselves.

They deducted ₹3,500 for deep cleaning even though I did not receive a properly cleaned flat when I moved in. Out of courtesy, I got the flat cleaned before leaving. I even got the refrigerator professionally cleaned through Snabbit and shared photographs as proof.

**Final Note:**
Rent here only after getting every commitment in writing, especially regarding deposits, painting, parking, cleaning, and move-out charges. If you're buying, thoroughly check for water leakage and seepage issues before making a decision.

text.text:
‼️ATTENTION‼️
Terrible experience at Aikya Roots. Avoid renting here if you are a bachelor or unmarried couple.

My girlfriend and I moved in after paying a ₹1.5 lakh deposit, signing a lease, and our nightmare began.

On the day of our moving in a random guy calling himself as building security employee told me unmarried couples were not allowed and this was the directive from the developer. I had been upfront about this with the broker and the flat owner who told me he had talked to the society and there wouldn’t be any issue. But now, as this building is still being managed by the developer’s team, they had an issue. Mind you, we have finalised this flat two weeks ago, submitted all our legal documents, signed lease, done police verification, and submitted the society’s move in form as well.

Then, when I demanded their rule in writing the building security refused and repeatedly demanded that I vacate immediately, despite the owner intervening multiple times and having discussions. The security later claimed the owner’s NOC was invalid, showed me an email haphazardly sent to the police, and displayed a statement saying security could use “any means necessary” to vacate tenants. All this because we were an unmarried couple.

The harassment continued throughout the day with security personnel repeatedly coming to my door, and the electricity to my flat was cut twice, the second time it remained cut until I left. All this happened while I was trying to work and coordinate with the owner, broker, and police.

After the entire day of trying to solve this by discussion, we abandoned the flat and booked an Airbnb at additional expense. I had to eat the loss on furniture rental, movers, and the struggle of finding a new flat.

Whatever dispute exists between the owner and building management, tenants should not be forced, threatened and harassed with immediate eviction, or have their electricity cut. If there was a rule about not allowing unmarried couples to live there, why was it not written out or why were we allowed to sign the lease, why did they not raise objection earlier only so we could have avoided all this harassment. And if any dispute with owner actually existed why was it not made public or pursued before.

This was an extremely stressful and awful first experience in Mumbai. Later on, even the owner delayed returning our deposit.

Anyways, if you want to rent/buy, take note, there are multiple PGs running in the building, no estimate on the Gas Pipeline connection and no direct water connection as of October 2026.
The building is still being managed by the developer’s team and amenities not open yet.
Do Clarify the rules directly with the building management in writing before renting here.

I recently visited Lodha Park in Worli, and I must say, it is truly impressive. The ambiance of the place is nothing short of luxurious, with meticulous attention to detail in every aspect. The entire building exudes a sense of elegance and comfort, making it one of the finest residential options in the area.

The cleanliness of Lodha Park is outstanding. The staff is exceptionally good, always alert and conscious of their duties. They ensure that every corner of the property is spotless and well-maintained, adding to the overall appeal of the place.

One of the standout features of Lodha Park is its extensive range of amenities. There are 3 towers spread across 17 acres of land. The cricket ground, club house, and luxurious pools provide residents with plenty of options for recreation and relaxation. The high-speed lifts make accessing the 65 floors quick and convenient, reflecting the modernity and efficiency of the building. Parking is ample and well-organized, which is a big plus for residents with vehicles.

The greenery around Lodha Park is another highlight. The lush surroundings and scenic beauty create a serene and peaceful environment, which is quite rare in a bustling city like Mumbai. It’s a perfect place for families to enjoy nature while being in the heart of the city. The canteen is an added convenience, offering a variety of food options for residents.

Overall, Lodha Park stands out as one of the best places for a family to live. The combination of luxury, cleanliness, excellent staff, and top-notch amenities makes it a premier choice in Worli.

The team was consistently professional, approachable, and responsive. Every query—small or large—was addressed patiently, communication was clear, and timelines were respected. There were no last-minute surprises or shifting goalposts, which went a long way in building trust.

The project itself is very well executed and competitively priced for the Bandra–BKC location. Construction quality, planning, and overall finishing reflect attention to detail and seriousness of intent. What truly stood out was that the project was delivered well before the committed timeline—something that has become increasingly rare in today’s real estate landscape.

Overall, this has been a genuinely positive and reassuring experience. Credit to the builder and the entire team for delivering on their promises with professionalism and integrity. I would comfortably recommend them to anyone looking for quality execution, reliability, and peace of mind in a home purchase.

text.text:
Sky City Mall by Oberoi Realty is a refreshing new addition to Mumbai’s western suburbs, blending modern design with premium retail and entertainment. Spread across a massive area with direct access to Devipada Metro station and the Western Express Highway, the mall is extremely well-connected and convenient to reach.

The ambience is upscale yet welcoming—spacious corridors, high ceilings, and plenty of natural light make it a comfortable space for shopping or just strolling around. The retail mix is impressive, featuring top international and Indian brands like Zara, H&M, Nike, Sephora, and Apple, along with upcoming premium dining options such as PF Chang’s and Pizza Express. The food court also offers a variety of casual and quick-bite outlets.

One of the biggest highlights is the INOX Megaplex, which houses IMAX, 4DX, and multiple advanced screen formats—making it a dream spot for cinema lovers in Borivali and beyond. Parking facilities are well managed, and connectivity to the metro is seamless.

Since the mall is newly opened , not all stores are operational yet, but more outlets are rolling out steadily. Despite that, it already feels like a lively lifestyle hub for the suburbs.
